name: Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd
tagline: Commodity-to-specialty chemicals + fertiliser group at a genuine inflection: record Q1 FY27 (EBITDA +65%, PAT +101%), two large projects commissioning Q2 FY27, first Equinor LNG supplies flowing, and a board-approved TAN/mining-chemicals demerger - offset by Rs 4.7k Cr net debt and cyclicality
business_overview: Deepak Fertilisers operates fertilizers, bulk chemicals (ammonia, nitric acid, IPA), mining/crop nutrition chemicals, and a growing specialty/explosives (Blasting Solutions, Croptek) business. A 15-year LNG supply deal with Equinor (0.65 MTPA) began deliveries in Q1 FY27 to lower ammonia feedstock cost. A Composite Scheme of Arrangement (board-approved 2026) will demerge the TAN / Mining Chemicals business out of Smartchem Technologies into Deepak Mining Services Pvt Ltd, and amalgamate Mahadhan Farm Technologies into Smartchem.
fundamentals_table: FY26 Rs 11,506 Cr (+12% YoY), PAT Rs 739 Cr (-22% YoY vs FY25 Rs 945 Cr); Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 3,256 Cr (+22% YoY)
EBITDA Rs 845 Cr (+65% YoY, record, ~26% margin); PAT Rs 490 Cr (+101% YoY)
Rs 4,719 Cr (Jun 2026); net debt/EBITDA 1.4x (from 2.86x); borrowings rose to Rs 5,670 Cr Mar 2026 (debt-funded capex); interest ~Rs 350-410 Cr/yr
FY26 CFO only Rs 206 Cr, FCF -Rs 1,363 Cr (peak capex year); FY25 CFO Rs 1,880 Cr
~18x trailing P/E (~9x on Q1 FY27 run-rate), P/B 2.65x, ~13-14x trailing EV/EBITDA
fundamentals_narrative: A large-cap with only ~11% 3-year ROCE/ROE and real leverage (Rs 4.7k Cr net debt, ~Rs 350-410 Cr annual interest), but the deep dive shows a genuine near-term inflection. FY26 was actually a down year (PAT Rs 739 Cr vs FY25 Rs 945 Cr) dragged by a weak H2, but Q1 FY27 was a record: revenue +22% YoY, EBITDA +65% to Rs 845 Cr (~26% margin vs ~12-14% in H2 FY26), PAT +101% to Rs 490 Cr - driven by stronger ammonia / mining-chemical realizations, first supplies under the 15-year Equinor LNG deal, and a richer specialty mix (Specialty + Croptek now 43% of Crop Nutrition revenue). Two large projects - Gopalpur TAN (376 KTPA, Rs 2,675 Cr, 96% complete) and Hazira/Dahej nitric acid (93% complete) - commission in Q2 FY27 with profit contribution from Q3 FY27 and ~80% TAN utilisation targeted by Q4 FY27. Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.4x, though mostly on the EBITDA surge rather than debt paydown (borrowings actually rose). Management flagged a possible monsoon-driven Q2 softening in mining/infra demand.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass. Stock is in the upper half of a Rs 866-1,681 52-week range after the record Q1 FY27 print; Emkay initiated Buy (Nov 2025) with ~39% upside.
sentiment_summary: Read most recent 50 of 399 posts (May 2025 to Aug 2026). Sentiment: a detailed, high-conviction bull thesis (commodity-to-specialty re-rating + sum-of-parts) built by one standout poster (r8b8), tempered by repeated capex delays and a weak Q4 FY26 print, with optimism returning strongly in the Q1 FY27 update. Deep dive (pass 1) cross-checked against FY26 audited results, the Q1 FY27 concall/slides, and BSE filings including the Composite Scheme of Arrangement.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users posted, but r8b8 stood out sharply (125 loves across 10 posts) with a detailed sum-of-parts thesis comparing Deepak's Blasting Solutions/explosives segment to Solar Industries; r8b8's model projected ~13% revenue CAGR and ~21% EBITDA CAGR FY26-29 - the Q1 FY27 print and the board-approved TAN demerger both move in that direction. Bear-leaning posts (Nirav_Mamniya, VALUE2017, Mehul1) flagged the ~Rs 400 Cr interest burden, repeated capex delays pushing benefits to FY28, and a weak Q4 FY26. Q1 FY27 (Mehul1, Aug 2026) reported margin improvement 'as per plan,' partly credited to the Equinor LNG deal.
bse_notes: Board-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement (2026): demerger of the TAN / Mining Chemicals business from Smartchem Technologies (STL) into Deepak Mining Services Pvt Ltd (DMSPL), plus amalgamation of Mahadhan Farm Technologies (MFTPL) into STL - subject to NCLT, shareholder, creditor and regulatory approvals. Earlier (Dec 2025): acquired 100% of Chardham Chemicals (explosives-licensing shell, no turnover) for ~Rs 121 Cr - a licences/expertise acquisition, flagged as unusual but not a red flag. No SEBI action, auditor qualification, or promoter pledge found; promoter holding 45.63% stable.
bull_case: Record Q1 FY27: revenue +22% YoY, EBITDA +65% to Rs 845 Cr (~26% margin), PAT +101% to Rs 490 Cr - a real inflection, part structural (Equinor LNG feedstock cost, specialty mix) and part cyclical (ammonia realizations)

Two large projects 93-96% complete and commissioning Q2 FY27 (Gopalpur TAN 376 KTPA; Hazira/Dahej nitric acid), profit contribution from Q3 FY27, ~80% TAN utilisation targeted by Q4 FY27 - dated, largely de-risked catalysts
Board-approved Composite Scheme demerging TAN / Mining Chemicals into a separate entity - the sum-of-parts value-unlock the community modelled is now an actual scheme in motion

15-year Equinor LNG deal is now live and management credits it for margin/cost visibility; specialty premiumisation continuing (Specialty+Croptek 43% of Crop Nutrition revenue, B2C 17% of Mining Chemicals)
On the Q1 FY27 run-rate the stock trades ~9x earnings and ~7x EV/EBITDA - cheap if the margin step-up proves even partly durable; net debt/EBITDA down to 1.4x
bear_case: FY26 full-year PAT fell 22% (Rs 739 Cr vs Rs 945 Cr) on a weak H2 - execution and earnings have been lumpy and cyclical, and one record quarter is not a run-rate
Net debt still Rs 4,719 Cr and borrowings actually rose to Rs 5,670 Cr (Mar 2026) to fund capex; FY26 CFO collapsed to Rs 206 Cr with FCF -Rs 1,363 Cr; interest ~Rs 350-410 Cr/yr
The 1.4x net debt/EBITDA is flattered by the EBITDA surge, not debt reduction - it would rise again if margins mean-revert
Management flagged a monsoon-driven Q2 FY27 slowdown in mining/infrastructure demand; ammonia / TAN pricing is a cycle, not a secular trend
The demerger needs NCLT + shareholder + creditor approvals - a 12-18+ month process with execution and terms risk
At ~Rs 18,000 Cr market cap the size itself requires a very large, durable specialty/TAN transition to clear this screen's asymmetric-upside bar - a 10x/100x outcome is not realistic here
verdict_headline: Deep dive materially de-risks the bull case - record Q1 FY27, near-dated project commissioning, and a board-approved TAN demerger - but size, Rs 4.7k Cr net debt and cyclicality keep it a Medium-High cyclical-plus-transition call, not a 10x story
verdict_reasoning: The prior 'catalysts real but execution inconsistent' read is improved: the Equinor LNG deal is live, Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record, and the two big projects are 93-96% done with contribution from Q3 FY27
The board-approved Composite Scheme is a concrete value-unlock mechanism (TAN / Mining Chemicals separation), no longer just a community sum-of-parts idea

But FY26 PAT declined, the balance sheet still carries Rs 4.7k Cr net debt funded by rising borrowings, the Q1 margin surge has a cyclical component, and at Rs 18,000 Cr the size math keeps thesis-fit 'neither'
Net: hold conviction at Medium-High - a well-set-up cyclical/transition story with dated catalysts and a real re-rating path, but not a high-conviction asymmetric bet
